title: Light takes the fastest path
lede: Light goes from A in air to B in glass, where it travels slower by the factor n. The curve below plots the total travel time for every crossing point on the surface.
notice: The curve has a single lowest point, and it sits directly below the crossing where the path is fastest.
At that point the ratio sin θ1 / sin θ2 equals n2 / n1. Anywhere else the two numbers differ.
A higher index bends the fastest path closer to the normal, so the ray spends less distance in the slow glass.
hint: Drag across the picture to move the crossing point, or press Snap to fastest.
